samples.text:
The line graph shows the average price of coffee in the world from 2014 to 2024, and the bar chart shows how much coffee four country exported in 2014 and 2024.

According to the line graph, the price of coffee was $4.4 per kg in 2014. It decreased to $3.5 in 2016 and continued to fall to $2.9 in 2018 and $2.6 in 2020, which was the lowest price. However, after 2020 the price increased very fast and it was $5.2 in 2022. In 2024 it reached $6.1 per kg, that is the highest in the period.

The bar chart shows that Brazil was the biggest exporter in both year. Its exports increased from 2.1 million tonnes to 2.6 million tonnes. Vietnam was in second place and its exports rised a little from 1.5 to 1.6 million tonnes. Colombia exports stayed the same at 0.7 million tonnes, and Ethiopia exported the least, but its exports doubled from 0.2 to 0.4 million tonnes.

In conclusion, the coffee price fell and then rose sharply, and most of countries exported more coffee in 2024.
samples.why: Basic overview given only at the end · all figures accurate but presented one by one · adequate but repetitive linking · simple vocabulary · noticeable errors in plurals, verb forms and relative clauses.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates changes in the average global price of coffee between 2014 and 2024, and the bar chart compares the quantity of coffee exported by four countries at the beginning and end of this period.

Overall, the price of coffee fell for six years and then rose sharply to its highest level in 2024. Brazil was the leading exporter in both years, and three of the four countries increased its exports.

In 2014, coffee cost an average of US$4.4 per kilogram. The price declined steadily over the next six years, reaching a low of US$2.6 in 2020. After this, however, it rebounded dramatically, doubling to US$5.2 in 2022 and climbing further to US$6.1 by 2024, which was around 40% higher than the starting price.

As regards to exports, Brazil shipped 2.1 million tonnes of coffee in 2014, and this rose to 2.6 million tonnes in 2024. Vietnam was the second largest exporter, although its exports grew only slightly, from 1.5 to 1.6 million tonnes. Colombia's exports remained unchanged at 0.7 million tonnes, while Ethiopia, despite being the smallest exporter, doubled the amount it sold abroad from 0.2 to 0.4 million tonnes.
samples.why: Clear overview of price trend and export leader · key features highlighted with apt comparisons (doubling, around 40%) · good cohesion · some less common vocabulary (rebounded, shipped) · two minor slips.

samples.text:
The line graph traces the average world price of coffee from 2014 to 2024, while the bar chart compares the coffee exports of four producing countries in the first and final years of that period.

Coffee prices followed a pronounced V-shaped pattern, bottoming out in 2020 before surging to a decade high. Over the same timeframe, Brazil consolidated its position as the largest exporter, and export volumes either rose or held steady in all four nations.

Starting at US$4.4 per kilogram in 2014, the world price fell continuously to US$2.6 in 2020, a drop of around 40%. The subsequent recovery was far steeper: within two years the price had doubled to US$5.2, and by 2024 it had reached US$6.1, well above its initial level.

Brazil's exports rose from 2.1 to 2.6 million tonnes, widening its lead over Vietnam, the second largest exporter, whose volumes barely changed (1.5 and 1.6 million tonnes). Colombia's exports remained static at 0.7 million tonnes. Ethiopia, by contrast, was by far the smallest exporter, yet it recorded the most rapid proportional growth, with its exports doubling from 0.2 to 0.4 million tonnes.
samples.why: Skilful overview summarising both visuals · accurate figures used selectively with precise derived comparisons · sophisticated cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary (bottoming out, consolidated) · varied, error-free sentence structures.
